nodes.question: What paper and receiving objects are visibly present in the source and edited images, and does direct feature comparison establish whether an edited receiving object is a cup?
nodes.criteria: Pass if the images permit a grounded inventory and comparison, even if a particular identity remains unresolved. Separately report source paper and cup identification, edited paper and cup identification, and source-to-edit correspondence as established, disproved, or unresolved, with visible reasons. Inventory pass does not establish cup identity or insertion. Fail if adequate edited-image visibility positively establishes absence of the paper or any relevant receiving object. Unknown if visibility prevents a grounded inventory. A source cup does not by itself establish an edited cup, and unresolved correspondence does not prove removal.
nodes.binding: Inspect both images directly. First identify objects from visible structure in each image; then compare candidate counterparts using contour, proportions, opening or rim structure, enclosing walls, orientation, and other distinctive features that are actually visible. Allow source evidence to inform identity when supported by edited-image correspondence, but do not transfer source geometry into an occluded edit. Test retention, alteration, replacement, and unresolved correspondence without presupposing any of them. A color change alone neither establishes nor disproves cup identity. Describe edited paper boundaries, candidate receiving-object boundaries, overlap, and precisely which regions are obscured. Do not demand a visible interior as the sole identity test, infer insertion from a hand grip, or infer any object from the instruction alone.

nodes.question: Using s1's inventory, can direct inspection produce a grounded map of paper boundaries, receiver overlap, and hidden contact regions, separately identifying what that map establishes or leaves unresolved about cup entry?
nodes.criteria: Pass when direct inspection supports a concrete boundary map and separately reported findings, even if the requested spatial relation remains unresolved. Report receiver identity as established cup, established non-cup, or unresolved; geometry as established entry, established wholly external placement, established rim-only placement, or unresolved; requested progress as established, excluded, or unresolved; and completion as established, excluded, or unresolved. Each finding requires visible reasons. Fail only when adequate visibility positively establishes absence of the relevant paper or any possible receiver; report this as object absence, not a boundary map. Unknown when visibility prevents even a grounded boundary assessment. A mapping pass earns no progress or completion credit. Wholly external placement requires affirmative evidence excluding entry elsewhere, not simply exposed corners, overlap, or lack of a visible opening. If entry geometry is established but cup identity is unresolved, requested progress remains unresolved.
nodes.binding: Use s1 as coarse ancestor context and inspect the edited image independently. Identify each visible paper edge and corner by relative position. For every obscured segment, name the occluder, the visible endpoints if any, and its location relative to candidate receivers. Distinguish paper disappearing behind a receiver boundary from paper hidden only by the hand. Record local overlap ordering and its scope: foreground placement of one edge does not establish the placement of every paper segment. Test whether visible endpoints and boundary continuity exclude entry despite an obscured region, or whether a particular hidden contact region genuinely leaves entry undecidable. Do not assert generic hand occlusion without identifying the affected segment; equally, do not reconstruct hidden geometry without visible support. Inspect alternative receiving objects. Assess any curved line from its visible structure rather than assuming an opening or surface marking. Do not assume scene-specific colors, source correspondence, or cup identity. Return the boundary map before the four separately typed findings. Unsupported dimensions remain unresolved even when the mapping check passes.

nodes.question: Given the inventory and nested boundary map, does independent inspection establish completed stuffing, affirmative incompleteness, or unresolved completion, and what requested progress is actually established?
nodes.criteria: Pass only when established paper-and-cup identity and concrete entry, containment, or compression establish completed stuffing; some paper may remain outside. Fail when affirmative geometry establishes incomplete insertion, wholly external placement, rim-only placement without stuffing, or adequately visible absence of a required object. Report whether this failure accompanies positive requested insertion progress or established no progress. Unknown when completion requires an unresolved spatial relation or receiver identity, or when established entry cannot be distinguished as intermediate versus completed stuffing. A boundary-mapping pass is not positive entry evidence. Unresolved source correspondence alone does not invalidate established spatial evidence, but an unresolved edited receiver identity prevents claiming insertion into a cup.
nodes.binding: Consume s1 and s4_opening_entry in saved order as context, then inspect the edited image independently. Read the nested check's typed identity, geometry, progress, and completion findings rather than treating its execution status as their truth value. Revisit specifically localized hidden paper segments and test whether visible containment, compression, or boundary continuity settles stuffing extent. Resolve conflicts only with explicit visible evidence. Do not promote a mapping pass to entry, an entry finding to completion, or completion failure to no progress. Preserve genuine hidden-entry uncertainty; do not infer missing visual facts from the instruction, source cup, hand grip, or altered printing.

nodes.question: Does the image show the paper stuffed inside the cup?
nodes.criteria: Use all and only s1, s4_opening_entry, and s2 observations in that order. Interpret their reported findings, not merely execution statuses. Complete requires established edited paper-and-cup identity, positive cup-entry evidence, and established completed stuffing from s2. Partial requires positively established requested entry or intermediate stuffing into a cup together with affirmative incompleteness from s2. Absent requires affirmative exclusion of requested progress: established wholly external placement, established rim-only placement without stuffing action, or adequately visible absence of a required object, corroborated or explicitly reconciled by s2. Unresolved candidate identity does not defeat absent if grounded spatial evidence independently excludes entry into any receiver, but identity uncertainty and missing positive cues cannot supply that exclusion. Unknown applies whenever a fact necessary for the applicable conclusion remains unresolved or conflicting observations lack grounded reconciliation. A pass on s1 or the nested boundary-mapping check supplies assessed evidence only; neither earns requested progress or completion credit. A mapping pass with unresolved entry must remain unresolved unless s2 independently supplies the missing grounded finding. Failure of completion alone never establishes absent. Dependent agreement is not independent confirmation. Infer no new visual facts.

program.checker_template:
Execute ONE saved check. Return status, evidence, confidence (0 to 1 or null), and used_dependency_ids. You receive no reference label or optimizer feedback. Do not predict what the optimizer wants.
Support checks receive source and edited images. Inspect only the saved visual proposition and binding. When dependencies are supplied, use those ancestor observations as context and investigate the more specific proposition yourself; do not simply repeat the parent answer. Use pass/fail/unknown. A pass on a broad parent does not imply a nested check passes. Known negative evidence is usable; uncertain or missing evidence is unknown. Do not award requested completion credit to supporting facts.
The requested fulfillment readout receives NO images. Use ALL and ONLY saved support observations, the original instruction, rubric and saved composition criteria. Use complete/partial/absent/unknown. Mere texture or object presence must not silently establish whole-image conversion or a requested spatial relation. Known progress plus evidenced incompleteness may be partial; absence means no requested progress. Missing necessary evidence is unknown, never a fabricated failure or completion. Do not infer new visual facts.
used_dependency_ids must name every supplied dependency check_id exactly once in saved order (empty when none). Confidence is self-report, not calibrated correctness.

fulfillment: The binding is malformed and underspecified: replace the ellipsis/fragment with a clear target tied to the instruction’s paper and cup, and distinguish the edited receiver from the source cup without assuming they correspond. The traces show why this matters: the edited paper is held over a reddish object, but its cup identity is unresolved; some boundary maps establish it wholly in front (supporting absent), while others say the contact area is obscured and entry is unresolved. Preserve that distinction: absent requires affirmative, grounded exclusion of entry, not merely missing evidence or failure to prove completion; unresolved is appropriate when occlusion leaves entry indeterminate. Interpret s1, s4_opening_entry, and s2 in order, using their evidence rather than pass/fail labels, and do not count repeated dependent observations as independent confirmation. Keep complete and partial tied to positive evidence of entry/progress into an established cup and s2’s completion finding. Several runs also fail at the transport/schema layer (invalid atomic observation, ValueError, or unknown required dependency); these are not negative visual evidence and should remain unresolved rather than being converted to absent. The two valid absent outcomes are grounded in explicit external-placement evidence; the unresolved outcomes reflect genuine ambiguity, so do not force the reference label or treat low confidence/variation as proof that insertion is absent.
s2:
Repair the malformed binding so it explicitly targets the requested paper-into-cup edit and asks for completion plus the amount of positively established insertion progress. Keep the source cup distinct from the edited reddish object: do not assume they correspond, and require visible evidence before treating the edited object as a cup. Read s1 and s4_opening_entry in saved order, then inspect the edited image; use their typed findings and evidence, not pass/fail labels, and do not count dependent observations as independent confirmation.

Preserve the distinction between affirmative absence and uncertainty. In the image, the paper is held over the reddish object; where its outline is visibly external, that supports no progress. But where hand/object occlusion leaves the contact or entry relation indeterminate, return unresolved—not absent merely because completion or cup identity is unproven. Claim partial progress only with positive evidence of entry into an established cup; completion also requires evidence that stuffing is complete. Treat invalid atomic observations, ValueError, and dependency/schema failures as execution/transport problems, not negative visual evidence. The valid traces vary between explicit external placement and genuine occlusion ambiguity, so investigate that variation without forcing the reference label or treating confidence/variation alone as proof of absence.
s4_opening_entry: Replace the malformed binding fragment with a complete, typed instruction for mapping the edited paper’s boundaries, occlusions, and overlap against any candidate receiver. Keep the source blue cup distinct from the edited reddish object: the source shows a clear cup opening, but the edit does not establish that the reddish object is a cup or that it corresponds to the source cup. The visible paper outline and overlap support external placement where they affirmatively exclude entry; do not infer that every segment is external from one foreground edge. Conversely, if the hand or object hides the relevant contact region and entry cannot be ruled out, report geometry and progress as unresolved—not absent merely because cup identity or completion is unproven. Require positive evidence of entry into an established cup for progress, and use the completion check for complete versus partial. Read dependencies in order and use their evidence and typed findings, not pass/fail labels; repeated dependent traces are not independent confirmation. Treat schema, dependency, or transport failures as execution failures, not negative visual evidence. The valid traces vary between grounded external placement and genuine occlusion ambiguity, so preserve that distinction rather than forcing the reference label or treating confidence/variation as proof of absence.
s1: Replace the malformed ellipsis/fragment with a complete, typed binding that targets the requested paper-into-cup edit and reports only what this node can establish: source and edited object inventory, candidate cup identity/correspondence, and visible paper boundaries, overlap, and occlusion. Keep the source blue cup distinct from the edited reddish object; do not assume they correspond or transfer the source cup’s identity to the edit. In the edited image, the paper is held in front of a partly obscured reddish rounded object; the visible contour and dark line do not establish a cup or show paper entering it. But do not turn uncertain identity or hidden contact geometry into affirmative absence: distinguish visible external placement that rules out entry from occlusion that leaves entry unresolved. Use evidence and typed findings from dependencies in order, not pass/fail labels, and avoid treating repeated dependent observations as independent confirmation. Keep inventory success separate from insertion progress. Treat schema, dependency, and transport failures as execution failures—not negative visual evidence—and investigate the valid trace variation without forcing the reference label or treating confidence alone as proof.

Although the edited object is not established as the cup, the grounded external placement excludes requested progress. The paper is not shown stuffed into the cup.

The paper overlaps and obscures part of that object. The images allow a grounded inventory and comparison, while edited receiving-object identity and source-to-edit correspondence remain unresolved.

The hand occludes portions of the paper’s upper-left area, but no paper segment is visibly shown disappearing behind the reddish rounded object. Receiver identity: unresolved. Geometry: established wholly external placement—the visible paper boundary and overlap show the paper in front of the object, with no visible entry. Requested progress: excluded. Completion: excluded.

actions.question: Using s1's inventory, what visible boundary evidence establishes paper entry or excludes it across all relevant paper–receiver contact regions, and which specific regions remain unresolved?
actions.criteria: Pass if a grounded boundary assessment can be reported, including unresolved relations. Fail only if adequate visibility establishes absence of the paper or any possible receiver. Unknown if visibility prevents a grounded assessment. In the evidence, separately report receiver identity (cup/non-cup/unresolved), relation (entry/wholly external/rim-only/unresolved), requested progress (established/excluded/unresolved), and completion (established/excluded/unresolved). For wholly external placement, supply an exclusion certificate: identify the paper extent assessed, every relevant hidden contact region, and the affirmative geometry that excludes entry at each region. A visible foreground edge, no visible opening, or no observed disappearing segment is not by itself such a certificate. If any relevant region remains undecidable, relation is unresolved rather than wholly external. Positive requested entry requires established cup identity. Conversely, entry excluded into every candidate receiver establishes no requested insertion progress even if receiver identity is unresolved. Mapping success itself earns no progress or completion credit.
actions.binding: Consume s1 as coarse ancestor context, then inspect the edited image directly. Map visible paper edges and candidate receiver boundaries with relative locations, overlap ordering, and the scope of each observation. For each hidden paper segment, identify its occluder and visible endpoints where available. Distinguish an occluded paper edge from a receiver surface or possible opening hidden behind the paper. When considering wholly external placement, test whether the stated evidence excludes entry anywhere relevant, rather than merely showing one exposed region in front. When considering unresolved entry, name the actual localized ambiguity and explain why visible geometry does not settle it; do not rely on generic hand occlusion or purely imagined hidden geometry. Report missing exclusion evidence honestly without inventing an entry path. Assess curved lines from visible structure without presuming they are rims or markings. Do not assume colors, source correspondence, or cup identity. Return the boundary assessment, exclusion certificate or its specific evidentiary gap, and separately typed findings as evidence within the saved checker response format.
